title: A small family of field extensions embeds in one common extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $J$ be a small set [def-weil-size-convention]. For every $j\in J$ let $L_j/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], with structural embedding $a_j:k\to L_j$. Then there are a field extension $K/k$ with structural embedding $b:k\to K$ and field embeddings $e_j:L_j\to K$ for all $j\in J$, such that $e_j\circ a_j=b$ for every $j$. No algebraicity or finiteness is assumed, and $J$ may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0CNJ, lemma-infinite-product-surjective, proof: 'Choose a huge field extension K/kappa(s)' into which each residue field embeds as a kappa(s)-extension.

proof.text: Form the coproduct A of the small diagram of commutative k-algebras L_j in CommAlg_k, with canonical k-algebra maps iota_j:L_j→A and structural map k→A. Such a coproduct exists because the category of commutative algebras over a commutative ring has colimits [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist].
Apply [lem-trf-family-tensor-nontrivial] to the family (L_j)_{j∈J}. It gives that A is nontrivial, including the empty-family case A≅k.

source.place: Tag 0CNJ, proof: choose a huge field extension containing all residue-field extensions

proof.text: Choose a maximal ideal I of A by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal], and put K=A/I. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field], K is a field; because the maximal ideal I is proper, the quotient K is nontrivial. Let b:k→K be the composite of the structural map k→A with the quotient map, and let e_j:L_j→K be the composite of iota_j with that quotient map.

source.place: Fields, Lemma 9.2, tag 0H7K: choose a maximal ideal and take the residue-field quotient

proof.text: The coproduct maps and the quotient map are k-algebra homomorphisms, so e_j∘a_j=b for every j. Each e_j is injective: a unital homomorphism from a field into a nontrivial ring has zero kernel, because a nonzero kernel element is invertible and would force 1=0. Thus K/k with b and the e_j satisfy the required conclusion. The construction also covers J=∅, when there are no e_j to specify.
